environment.postgresql: PostgreSQL 18.3 server (local, port 55431, user postgres, trust authentication), psql 18.3; earlier password-authentication runs used a second local 18.3 server with scram-sha-256

procedure: Exported the lab files of the named commit with git archive into uncommitted private staging outside the repository and replaced tests/relational/SchemaTest.java with the corrected file whose sha256 is recorded below (student inserts now give explicit ids with OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE).
Ran the setup command mvn -q dependency:go-offline in starter/.
Ran mvn -q -o test on the shipped starter.

Replaced only starter/schema.sql with privately staged completed schemas whose students.id was, in turn, integer PRIMARY KEY, integer GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY and bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, and ran mvn -q -o test for each with PGHOST, PGPORT and PGUSER pointing at the local server.
Ran the same command with two nonconforming GENERATED ALWAYS identity schemas (no UNIQUE on email; text name with no length limit).
As a regression check, ran the previous SchemaTest.java (sha256 f631bff32e5e00e7f595855fcbdf9c0bd2faafc1076e479a61541a4d7368723a) against the GENERATED ALWAYS identity schema.
result: Completed schemas: mvn -q -o test exited 0 for the plain integer, GENERATED BY DEFAULT identity and GENERATED ALWAYS identity ids; surefire report for each: Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0.
starterRun: On the shipped starter, mvn -q -o test exits 1 and fails all five declared failingTests (Tests run: 5, Failures: 5), each with a stable message naming the missing table or column.
cleanup: Every run created only starter/target inside the lab and one uniquely named relational_design_lab_<12 hex> database, which it dropped at the end; afterwards no relational_design_lab_% database remained and starter/target/lab-database.txt was gone. The private staging copy and its server were then removed.
otherSystems: Password authentication was run on macOS against a scram-sha-256 server: through a PGPASSFILE password file (exit 0, 5 passed), with no password available (stable 'Could not reach PostgreSQL' setup error), and through PGPASSWORD (exit 0, 5 passed); a socket-directory PGHOST gave the stable 'PGHOST is set to ... which is not a host name' error. Linux and Windows runs are not yet recorded and remain unverified; CI covers Ubuntu (lab-contract section 10).
testScope: The public tests check table and column names, that each column's type is a suitable kind for its criterion, which inserts and deletes PostgreSQL accepts or rejects (by SQLSTATE), and the values it stores (current-time default, exact two-decimal grade); they do not check constraint names, statement layout or one particular type spelling.
variantRuns: GENERATED ALWAYS identity regression: the previous SchemaTest.java exited 1 with 4 failures ('cannot insert a non-DEFAULT value into column "id"'); the corrected file exits 0 with Tests run: 5, Failures: 0. Nonconforming GENERATED ALWAYS identity schemas: without UNIQUE email, exit 1 with only task2Students failing ('no two students share an email'); with an unlimited text name, exit 1 with only task2Students failing ('a name has at most 100 characters'). Earlier runs at 1ff0de5b39b45b1514b52430a58fd4f551772396 also covered an alternative suitable schema (exit 0) and three nonconforming task-5 schemas (each exit 1 with only task5EnrollmentDefaults failing).
collisionSafety: Recorded at 1ff0de5b39b45b1514b52430a58fd4f551772396 with byte-identical tests/relational/LabDatabase.java: a pre-existing relational_design_lab database and marker row survived every run, and a forced first-name collision left the pre-created relational_design_lab_000000000000 database intact while the run used a second generated name.
